title: Canonical map to the fraction submonoid localization
statement: Let $P$ be a commutative monoid, written multiplicatively, let $S\subseteq P$ be a submonoid, and let $i:P\to P^{\rm gp}$ be the canonical Grothendieck group map. For the fraction submonoid $P_S=\{i(p)i(s)^{-1}:p\in P,\ s\in S\}$ [def-trf-monoid-face-localization], define the canonical monoid homomorphism $j_S:P\to P_S$ by $j_S(p)=i(p)=i(p)i(1)^{-1}$. Thus $j_S$ is $p\mapsto p/1$, with codomain membership witnessed by numerator $p$ and denominator $1\in S$. No integrality, finiteness, saturation, or face hypothesis is needed to define this map.

source.place: Exposé VIII 3.1.2, printed p. 98 (localization inside the group completion and its canonical monoid map).
